note: The pinned artefacts of the ESP32 machine path: the emulator, the chip's own mask ROM, and the MicroPython image it boots. Re-verify with the sha256 above; never patch in place.

artifacts.name: esp32sim (WebAssembly build, with the GPIO, I2C and SPI seams)
artifacts.note: The emulator: it boots the chip's own mask ROM, the second-stage bootloader and an unmodified application. Unofficial and not affiliated with Espressif. This build carries the three local patches in ../patches/: the GPIO seam, which adds the three exports a bench needs to read what the chip drives and to drive what it reads; the I2C seam, which lets the host answer the chip's I2C controller so the bench's devices are on the bus the firmware talks on; and the SPI seam, which does the same for the chip's SPI master, with the levels of the D/C and chip-select lines the host has to know about. scripts/build-esp32-wasm.mjs rebuilds it from upstream and the patches; the hash above is the toolchain's output, and the host family changes it.

artifacts.name: MicroPython (ESP32 port, ESP32_GENERIC variant)
artifacts.note: The same MicroPython release the RP2 port is pinned to. A combined bootloader, partition table and application, flashed at 0x1000.

artifacts.name: ESP32 mask ROM (rev 3.0)
artifacts.note: Espressif's own mask ROM, the first thing the chip runs. The image the emulator boots from; rev 3.0 is the silicon the DevKit V1 carries.
